findings.description: The inline user policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:* and cloudwatch:* on Resource "*", giving the deploy user full control over compute, storage, serverless and monitoring across the entire account. Compromise of this identity yields near-administrative access, including data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and lambda code modification for privilege escalation.

A permanent IAM access key is created in Terraform for a highly privileged user; the secret is stored in Terraform state in plaintext (no PGP key supplied), so anyone with state file access obtains working credentials. Static keys also never rotate.

No pgp_key is configured, so Terraform stores the unencrypted `secret` attribute in state; the encrypted_secret output referenced elsewhere will be null/empty, indicating the credential is held in cleartext rather than encrypted.
The output "svc_deploy_key_material" exposes access key secret material and is not marked sensitive, so it is printed to the console and CI logs during apply and readable via `terraform output`.

A standalone IAM user with programmatic credentials is used for deployment instead of an assumable role with temporary credentials, and force_destroy=true allows silent removal of its keys/attachments. This creates a long-lived, broadly privileged identity outside of any MFA or session-based control.
